text:
elena: Quick follow-up on model pinning metadata — Im proposing a small "gating" shim on rollout manifests so clients can opt into stricter stability checks. Want to surface tradeoffs before we update the API.

TJ: Can you sketch an example payload?

elena: Sure — thinking something like:
```json
{
  "model_pin": "redwood-7b:v2",
  "rollout": {
    "strategy": "canary",
    "gating": {
      "compat_level": "strict",
      "min_success_rate": 0.995,
      "grace_window_s": 3600
    }
  }
}
```

sophie: Hmm. Two immediate concerns: 1) how do older clients react to unknown "gating"? 2) who enforces compat_level? runtime or control plane? :thinking:

raj: Runtime should be enforcement point for latency/circuit-breaker semantics, control plane for policy. If runtime enforces compat_level strictly we need a clear fallback when an expected variant isn't available.

tj: For backwards compatibility we could default compat_level to "permissive" if missing. New manifests set "compat_level" explicitly. That avoids breaking old clients.

elena: Good — that matches my intent. Also plan to add a short migration: any manifest without gating stays permissive. We only flip enforcement once the control plane flags the tenant as "gating-enabled".

sophie: What about rollout TTL/eviction interplay? If a canary fails and we backoff, do we auto-evict pins that were created because of gating? We need a consistent state machine.

raj: Suggestion: annotate pin leases with a "gating_origin" tag and a tombstone_reason enum so ops can query and reconcile. Example: tombstone_reason: "gating-failed".

elena: I like that. Also telemetry: we should emit a metric per gating evaluation (pass/fail, latency delta, token-cost-diff). That helps product decide default thresholds.

deploy-bot: Canary job 3623 queued for tenant: acme-inc — will run gating checks after 10m.

tj: One last engineering tradeoff — adding these fields increases schema surface. Do we want a small extension (gating object) or a more generic "annotations" bag to avoid churn?

sophie: Annotations are flexible but make validation weaker. I prefer the dedicated gating object so we can validate and evolve with clear fields.

elena: OK let's capture that: dedicated gating object, default permissive behavior for old manifests, control-plane toggle per-tenant, runtime enforcement with defined fallback, pin lease annotation for tombstones, and telemetry counters. I'll draft a short RFC addendum and link a migration playbook.

raj: +1. Can you flag any rollout APIs we should version bump? I think the client SDK should accept the gating object but ignore if feature disabled.

elena: Will do. Action items: elena -> publish RFC addendum today; tj -> mock client update; sophie -> validate runtime gating paths; raj -> ops reconciliation query.

sophie: cool. Thanks.

elena: Thanks all :thumbsup:
